prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1039; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a sideswipe that occurred while the insured was changing lanes. The claimant reports neck pain with whiplash symptoms and is not represented by counsel.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant's vehicle at the scene and describes the lane-change contact as reported. Statements from two independent witnesses match this account.

Entry 3: Photos of the vehicle show damage on the rear quarter panel consistent with the impact described by all parties. The other driver has also confirmed how the collision happened.

Entry 4: Spoke with the claimant, who gave the same account of the accident as in the first contact. The reported whiplash injury is plausible for a collision of this type.

Entry 5: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that the policy was in force on the date of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the vehicle damage predates coverage.

Entry 6: Checked prior claims and medical history. No earlier injury to the neck or upper back is known, and no earlier damage to the vehicle appears in our records.

Entry 7: Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this injury. Requested updated records from the treating provider to confirm the ongoing care plan.

Entry 8: Received the treatment records and reviewed the billing against the documented care. The course of treatment is consistent with the diagnosis, though the duration is longer than average.

Entry 9: File is progressing toward evaluation. Liability appears clear based on the police report, witness statements, photos, and the other driver's account, and the claim will proceed to settlement review.
